input.command:
git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent writes

The cache store used plain fs::write for both content and metadata
files, which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes write to
the same cache directory simultaneously, a reader could observe a
partially-written file, producing corrupted JSON parse errors.

Replace fs::write with write-to-temp-then-rename, which is atomic
on POSIX filesystems. Also make load() resilient to pre-existing
corruption by returning None (and cleaning up) rather than
propagating parse errors.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent writes

The cache store used plain fs::write for both content and metadata
files, which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes write to
the same cache directory simultaneously, a reader could observe a
partially-written file, producing corrupted JSON parse errors.

Replace fs::write with write-to-temp-then-rename, which is atomic
on POSIX filesystems. Also make load() resilient to pre-existing
corruption by returning None (and cleaning up) rather than
propagating parse errors.
EOF
)"

git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent writes

The cache store used plain fs::write for both content and metadata
files, which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes write to
the same cache directory simultaneously, a reader could observe a
partially-written file, producing corrupted JSON parse errors.

Replace fs::write with write-to-temp-then-rename, which is atomic
on POSIX filesystems. Also make load() resilient to pre-existing
corruption by returning None (and cleaning up) rather than
propagating parse errors.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git add src/cache/store.rs && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption from concurrent writes

The cache store used plain fs::write for both content and metadata
files, which is not atomic. When multiple bivvy processes write to
the same cache directory simultaneously, a reader could observe a
partially-written file, producing corrupted JSON parse errors.

Replace fs::write with write-to-temp-then-rename, which is atomic
on POSIX filesystems. Also make load() resilient to pre-existing
corruption by returning None (and cleaning up) rather than
propagating parse errors.
EOF
)"
